cards.title: GLM-5.3: Z.ai Reaches Coding Frontier with Post-Training Alone, No New Base Model
cards.why_it_matters: As an AI/ML engineer, understanding how a ~750B-parameter model built purely on extended post-training matches or beats Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6-Sol on agentic coding benchmarks is a direct signal about where capability gains are coming from right now.
cards.summary: Z.ai's GLM-5.3 uses the same base model as GLM-5.2 but with substantially extended post-training — more RL environments, more diverse tasks, more compute on them. At roughly 750B parameters (about a third of Kimi K3), it surpasses Kimi K3 on many agentic coding benchmarks and matches or beats Claude Fable 5 and GPT-5.6-Sol on some. Z.ai attributes gains to RL scale, not distillation. Open weights coming to Hugging Face in two weeks.

cards.title: HF Hub Summer 2026: Chinese Labs Dominate Frontier Open Weights, U.S. Shifts to Hardware-Vendor Models
cards.why_it_matters: This structural snapshot of open-model publishing directly shapes which base models and ecosystems an AI/ML engineer should track and build on.
cards.summary: HF repositories grew from 2.43M to 2.96M models and 711K to 1M datasets. Chinese labs (Moonshot, MiniMax, Xiaomi, Z.ai) released frontier open models ranging 754B–2.78T parameters monthly, while U.S. labs mostly stayed under 130B outside NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra (561B) and Thinking Machines' Inkling (952B). AMD and NVIDIA now lead U.S. new model releases (200+ repos each), displacing Google and Meta. Most U.S. releases above 100B are conversions or fine-tunes of Chinese models.

cards.title: Exact Calibration of Multi-Label Jaccard Loss Requires Exponentially Many Prediction Coordinates
cards.why_it_matters: For an ML researcher working on structured prediction or segmentation, this result sets a hard theoretical floor on surrogate loss design for IoU objectives and offers two concrete polynomial-dimension approximation alternatives.
cards.summary: For s-label Jaccard (IoU) loss, the convex calibration dimension is bounded between 2^(s-1) and 2^s−1, meaning any exactly calibrated convex surrogate needs exponentially many output coordinates. Two polynomial alternatives are provided: an (s²+1)-dimensional F1-to-Jaccard transfer with asymptotic regret at most 3−2√2, and a MinHash square-loss surrogate with dimension O((s²+s·log(1/ρ))/α²) (signed variant: O((s+log(1/ρ))/α²)) achieving regret floor α with probability 1−ρ.

cards.title: QuoteBench: Shell Quoting/Parsing Boundaries Cut LLM Agent Success by 55–73 Points, Frontier Models Adapt Unevenly
cards.why_it_matters: Any engineer deploying LLM coding agents needs to know that matched-score benchmarks hide catastrophic execution-path failures that only emerge when the full generation-to-shell transport stack is tested.
cards.summary: QuoteBench tests 8 agent configurations on 56 one-shot Bash tasks across 14 incident-derived families, inserting a single unescaped parser between generation and execution. Replaying identical outputs through that parser drops success rates by 55.4–73.2 percentage points. Disclosing the boundary recovers 30.4–60.7 points for 6 configurations but zero or negative for 2. GPT-5.6-sol's −3.6-point matched gap hides −64.3 points of damage and +60.7 points of recovery. Model rankings change under deployment configuration, with at least one unambiguous reversal among 26 comparable pairs.
